name: ANSI/IEEE Inductive proximity switch form
summary: IEEE-library form of inductive proximity switch: an inductive proximity switch detects a documented target without a mechanical contact actuator.
description: This reference locates inductive proximity switch in Autodesk's IEEE-oriented inductive switches family. An inductive proximity switch detects a documented target without a mechanical contact actuator. The schematic shows its supply and output arrangement, while target distance and material are specified elsewhere. The public library uses HPX1I for its horizontal representation; this is a vendor block name, not an IEEE standards symbol number.

Read the operating mechanism and the contact reference state together. Cross-reference every associated contact to the same device and show which movement, signal or reset changes its condition; the symbol alone does not establish the complete switching sequence.

Distinguish a two-wire output path from a three-wire supply and signal arrangement. An inductive proximity switch detects an electromagnetic target interaction, not capacitance or an optical beam. The linked functional counterpart explains the same operating role in its own drawing context; agreement of every detailed convention mark is not asserted.
